section_1_complete_textbook_notes.chapter_overview: This chapter introduces precise geometric drawing using ruler, compass, and set-squares. It covers drawing circles of specified radii, locating center points, transferring segment distances accurately, and constructing perpendicular lines and rectangles.

detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: A circle is a closed plane curve formed by all points equidistant from a fixed center point O. Radius r is the fixed distance from center to boundary. Diameter d = 2r.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: The set of all points in a plane equidistant (radius r) from a fixed center point O.
mathematical_definitions.example: Circle drawn with 4 cm compass opening.

bisector_construction_mastery.explanation: Perpendicular bisector of segment AB is constructed by drawing arcs of equal radius > AB/2 from endpoints A and B. Angle bisectors divide angle theta into two theta/2 angles using intersecting arcs.

section_2_step_by_step_algorithms.method_name: Constructing a Circle of Given Radius r
step_by_step_instructions: Step 1: Mark center point P on paper.
Step 2: Set compass span to radius r against a ruler.
Step 3: Fix compass needle firmly at P and rotate pencil 360°.

model_textbook_example.problem: Construct a circle of radius 4 cm centered at P.
working_steps: Pivot needle at P and rotate pencil tip.

section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.question_text: What shape is formed by all points located exactly 4 cm away from point P?
section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.complete_solution: A circle of radius 4 cm centered at P.

section_4_complete_textbook_exercise_sol.question_text: Draw a rectangle with sides 6 cm and 4 cm using ruler and set-square.
solution_steps: Use set-square to construct 90° perpendiculars at A and B.
Mark 4 cm along both perpendiculars to locate D and C.
